tossups.text: The first Westerner known to have engaged in this literary genre is the Dutchman Hendrik Doeff, and R. H. Blyth later popularized it in the English-speaking world. One of these describing fireflies flying away was written by Ueshima Onitsura, and another master of this told of a frog jumping in "an ancient pond" with a splash. He also popularized this style that contains kireji, a cutting word, as well as kigo, a seasonal reference, and consists of seventeen mora. For 10 points, name this style of Japanese poetry that in English contains lines of five, seven, and five syllables.

In the final act of this work, a main character cries that "the world is lit by lightning" and that "time is the longest distance between two places," indicating that he must blow out a metaphorical candle to rid himself of the memories of his sibling. Instead of learning to be a typist, that sibling wanders to a greenhouse named the Jewel Box, even though she wears a bulky brace on her leg. Her teenage crush, Jim O'Connor, comes over and they dine by candlelight, but he accidentally breaks her heart when he reveals he is engaged and breaks her favorite figurine, a unicorn. For 10 points, Amanda goads Tom Wingfield into finding his shy sister Laura a "gentleman caller" in what play by Tennessee Williams?

A letter to this philosopher was the first to ask if a blind person experienced at touching objects could recognize the objects upon being granted sight. This recipient of the Molyneux (MOHL-in-oo) Problem wrote that properties such as color and texture are "secondary" in a book that denies the existence of "innate ideas." This author of An Essay Concerning Human Understanding endorsed slavery in his constitution for the Province of Carolina, despite his 1689 defense of natural rights. For 10 points, name this author of the Second Treatise on Government.

This author was inspired by the fairy tale "The Fisherman and His Wife" to write a novel criticized by feminists called The Flounder. A novel by this author includes the jazz musician Klepp and a man who dies after swallowing a Nazi pin. An Iron Cross is stolen by Joachim Mahlke [YO-uh-kim MALL-kuh] in this author's novel Cat and Mouse. The protagonist of a novel by this author is accused of Sister Dorothea's murder, is able to shatter glass with his voice, and stops growing at the age of three when he receives the title item. For 10 points, name this author of the Danzig Trilogy, which includes The Tin Drum.

The background of this painting shows a floating platform in front of Catalonian cliffs. A dead tree projects from a larger platform in the near left of this painting, and a face-down object in the lower left corner swarms with ants. A monstrous face, a self-portrait of the artist, spans the middle of this painting, and is draped with an unusual timepiece. Featuring soft clocks, for 10 points, name this painting by Salvador Dali.

In this part of a larger organ, a controversial "backwash" form of inflammation may follow from a procedure called I·P·A·A that makes part of it into a J-shaped pouch. It's not in the kidney, but this part of a larger organ expresses a complex of cubilin and amnionless called cubam. Cholestyramine ("KOH-luh-STYE-ruh-meen") can be used to treat diarrhea that results from re·sectioning of this structure, which is where the re·absorptive phase of entero·hepatic circulation occurs. Nod2 ("nod-two") suppresses bacterial colonization of this structure, which has the highest density of Paneth ("PAH-nett") cells. Bile salts and the complex of intrinsic factor and cobalamin are mainly absorbed from this structure. Most Peyer's patches are found in this structure. This structure is the one most often affected by Crohn's disease, and the ICV limits reflux into it from the cecum ("SEE-kum"). For 10 points, name this structure that follows the jejunum ("jee-JOO-num") as the final part of the small intestine.

Explored in the late 1730s by Sieur de la Verendrye, this state receives most of its irrigaton and power from the Garrison Dam on the Missouri River. Home to the International Peace Garden, Theodore Roosevelt National Park, and Fort Lincoln, it is currently considering changing its name to improve its image to tourists. For 10 points-name this state located between Montana and Minnesota.

A fallen angel must accomplish penance in this man's oratorio Paradise and the Peri, and his only opera was entitled Genoveva. Eighteen solo piano pieces are found in this man's collection Dances of the League of David. One of this composer's works includes sections titled "Of Foreign Lands and People" and "Blind Man's Bluff." In addition to Scenes from Childhood, other works of his include Papillons and Symphonic Etudes. In 1841, his First Symphony premiered with the nickname "Spring," while his Third Symphony in E-Flat was nicknamed "Rhenish." For ten points, name this German composer who married a fellow musician named Clara.

This economic quantity is increased in quantitative easing while the Federal Reserve lowers the yield of Treasury notes. On a graph of price vs. quantity, this quantity's curve slopes upward, because more good are produced at higher prices. For ten points, name this economic concept, the amount of a good that can be produced, often compared against a good's demand.

A painting by this man includes a darkened version of Francesco Furini's Lot and his Daughters in the background and includes a hook-nosed woman with bare arms she was so proud of that she banned gloves in her court. Theophile Gautier said that a painting by this man depicted "the corner baker and his wife after they have won the lottery", due to their vacuous facial expressions. A dagger-wielding man unhorses a turban-wearing soldier in a painting by this man inspired by the same conflict that spawned a painting lit primarily by a huge square lantern, in which a white-shirted man throws his hands into the air. The Peninsular War inspired this man's paintings of the events of the second and third of May, 1808. For 10 points, name this court painter to Charles IV of Spain, whose Black Paintings include Saturn Devouring His Son.
acceptableAnswers: Francisco Jose de Goya y Lucientes

tossups.text: This poet wrote the line, "I cannot bring a world quite round/Although I patch it as I can." Harriet Monroe cut a stanza by this poet that said, "Divinity must live within herself." Helen Vendler's book On Extended Wings takes its title from a work by this poet that repeats, "Death is the mother of beauty." This poet wrote, "let be be the finale of seem" in a poem possibly set at a funeral that describes a woman's "horny feet" protruding and begins, "call the roller of big cigars." For 10 points, name this poet of "The Emperor of Ice-Cream."
this structure is essential for tonsils and malt. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this lymph-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The lymph is a key component of the Immune system, involved in tonsils and malt.

tossups.text: This scientist included "force", "diffusion", and "collision" terms in one equation to describe a distribution function's time evolution. Thermodynamic beta equals the reciprocal of temperature times this scientist's namesake constant. Three-half T times this scientist's namesake constant equals a monatomic ideal gas's kinetic energy. This scientist had his definition of entropy as proportional to the log of the number of microstates engraved on his tombstone. This scientist and Maxwell name a distribution describing an ideal gas's particle speeds. For 10 points, what Austrian scientist's namesake constant is equal to R over Avogadro's number and is symbolized k-sub-B?

Hindu participants in these events walk around a fire seven times. Some Muslim scholars hold that these events can be undone by saying "talaq" three times. Jesus turned water into wine at one of these events in Cana. Some Mormon fundamentalists still practice the plural form of this practice, in which men undergo it multiple times with different women. For 10 points, what events usually feature a bride and a groom?

This believer in a human faculty called the "natural light" made an error of reasoning in accepting what he called "clear and distinct" truths; that error is his namesake "circle." He wrote in letters to Princess Elizabeth of Bohemia that the "seat of the soul" might be the pineal gland. This tutor to Princess Christina of Sweden proposed that a malicious demon might be altering all his sensory input, and argued that the mind interacts non-materially with the body, starting off his namesake "dualism." For 10 points, name this author of Discourse on Method, a Frenchman who invented a coordinate graphing system and said "I think, therefore I am."

One building in this city is home to six captive ravens, which are said to guard the security of the nation. Piccadilly Circus is located in this city's West End. This city, home to landmarks such as Trafalgar Square and Hyde Park, also contains the Tower Bridge, which crosses the River Thames. For 10 points, what city, home to Buckingham Palace and the British Museum, is the capital of the United Kingdom?

According to Betz's Law, the maximum power that can be extracted from this phenomenon is 16/27 of the total amount present in these phenomena. Latent heat polynyas can be produced by the katabatic form of this phenomenon, which occurs due to gravity. This phenomenon reverses direction at the boundaries between the Hadley and Ferrel cells, which occurs at the horse latitudes. The speed of this phenomenon is measured with an anemometer and can be classified by the Beaufort scale. For 10 points, name this meteorological phenomenon caused by differences in air pressure that makes air move.

In a seminal 1995 paper, Samuel Messick argued that traditional understandings of this concept were incomplete due to not accounting for an understanding of score meaning, instead advocating for a popular 6 "aspect" view of it. Meehl and Cronbach presented a framework for interpreting one type of this concept for evidence interpretation in a 1955 paper critiquing contemporary personality tests. The degree to which a result illustrates cause and effect or can be generalized is measured with the internal and external type of this concept respectively. A type of this concept that measures the degree to which a measure represents the needed facets of a variable is known as the logical or content type. Other notable subtypes of this concept are the criterion and construct variety. For 10 points, name this concept central to psychometrics, the degree to which a test measures the construct it is intended to.

Credit for the resolution of this conflict is often given to Louis-Auguste de Breteuil, who helped produce an agreement involving the cession of Bayreuth and Ansbach. Ernst von Louden and Franz von Lacy led the army of the nation that had gained Mindelheim in a secret treaty . Catherine the Great and Louis XVI were neutral peace brokers for the end of this conflict, which began when the Sulzbach line stood to fill in after Maximilian III's death ended his branch of the Wittelsbach line, leading Charles Theodore's claim to be challenged by Charles of Zweibrucken at the urging of Frederick the Great. FTP, the Treaty of Teschen ended what largely bloodless conflict, nicknamed the Potato War, and fought over a state in southern Germany?

1. To determine if a Fourier series has this property, the Dini-Lipschitz criterion is used. The Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem states that every bounded sequence in Rn has a subsequence that has this property. A Cauchy sequence has this property if its metric space is complete. A geometric series has this property if the absolute value of the common ratio is less than one. The harmonic series does not have this property. For 10 points, name this property of a sequence or series that approaches a finite limit, contrasted with divergence.

parts.text: Name this novel narrated by Pip, who visits the wealthy Miss Havisham at Satis House and falls in love with Estella, her cold and dismissive adoptive daughter.

This English author wrote Great Expectations. He also wrote about Ebenezer Scrooge's encounters with the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Christmas Present, and Christmas Yet to Come in his novella A Christmas Carol.
Dickens set his novel A Tale of Two Cities in London and this French city. Quasimodo serves as the bellringer for a cathedral in this city in Victor Hugo's The Hunchback of Notre Dame.

bonuses.leadin: The narrator of this novel steals food and a file for Abel Magwitch, an escaped convict whom he meets in the village churchyard. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this play about Hamm and Clov, who are unable to stand and sit respectively.
This other play by the same author features Vladimir and Estragon performing the title action. It also features the characters Lucky and Pozzo.
Endgame and Waiting for Godot are works of this Irish playwright, who also wrote Krapp's Last Tape.

bonuses.leadin: Negg and Nell live in trash cans after losing their legs in a bicycle accident. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this philosopher who formulated analysis through deconstruction.

Derrida wrote of deconstruction in this 1967 book, which was translated into English by Gayatri Spivak. This book lays out a history of writing, and a sentence from it has been translated to "there is nothing outside the text".
Derrida was an Algerian-born poststructuralist social critic who moved to this country. Other social critics from this country include Roland Barthes, Claude Levi-Strauss, and Michel Foucault.

bonuses.leadin: This author coined the term "différance," with an "a". For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this protagonist of Things Fall Apart who hangs himself rather than go to trial in a colonial court.
This author of Things Fall Apart also wrote about Okonkwo's grandson Obi's eventual acceptance of a bribe in No Longer at Ease.
Achebe criticised this author's Heart of Darkness in his lecture titled "An Image of Africa" for its support of colonialism and othering of African people and cultures.

bonuses.leadin: This man participates in the ritual killing of his ward Ikemefuna. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this South Dakota sculpture that shows four heads carved into a mountain.
Mount Rushmore was started by this sculptor who died in 1941, mid-sculpture.
Borglum also worked on Stone Mountain, a monument to Robert E. Lee, Stonewall Jackson and Jefferson Davis in this U.S. state.

bonuses.leadin: This sculpture is sometimes called the Shrine of Democracy. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this property that exists "intrinsically" in certain folded proteins, which have higher flexibility and more structural instability than globular or fibrous types.

Disordered regions disfavor amino acids with this property, such as phenylalanine and valine, which have non-polar hydrocarbon side chains and are usually buried in the core where they cannot contact water.
Annular lipid shells solvate the hydrophobic faces of members of this group of "integral" polytopic proteins that span the depth of the lipid bilayer and come in single-pass and multi-pass types.

bonuses.leadin: This property of proteins can be predicted by a high Debye-Waller temperature factor, or B-factor, which describes the mean-square displacement of their constituent atoms. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this city, built around Skanderbeg Square, which houses an art museum in a former Cold War bunker called Bunk'Art.
A valley northwest of Tirana provides views of this body of water, which is connected to the Ionian Sea by the Strait of Otranto. The cities of Split and Dubrovnik lie on this body of water.
Tirana is the capital of this Balkan country to the north of Greece. Like the ethnically similar Kosovo, this majority-Muslim country is one of the world's most pro-American populations.

bonuses.leadin: This city's Et'hem Bey Mosque is named for the Bejte poet who oversaw its completion. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Judith leads the servant Abra, who is carrying the severed head of Holofernes (hoh-loh-FUR-nayz), in the 1472 pendant painting The Return of Judith to Bethulia, by this artist of and The Birth of Venus.
acceptableAnswers: Alessandro di Mariano di Vanni Filipepi

parts.text: This Baroque tenebrist of The Calling of St. Matthew created two long-lost versions of Judith Beheading Holofernes, one of which was rediscovered in 1950 and the other in 2014.
This painter's 1614 Judith Beheading Holofernes is often interpreted as a response to her own assault by Agostino Tassi.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these painters who depicted the biblical heroine Judith.

parts.text: Name this American behaviorist, who famously studied operant conditioning. His writings include a depiction of a theoretical cooperative community, written as a "sequel" to a work by Henry David Thoreau.
Subtitled "Life in the Woods", this is that aforementioned Thoreau work. It details the author's life as a hermit near the titular pond.
B.F. Skinner often studied this bird's tendencies toward superstition. He also devised a weapon guided by placing these birds in missile cones.

bonuses.leadin: This psychologist was also a noted inventor, creating the air-crib to assist in raising babies. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Who is this jazz saxophonist who was nicknamed "Bird"?
Parker is associated with this fast form of jazz popularized by himself and Dizzy Gillespie.
This idiosyncratic pianist, composer of "'Round Midnight," is another founder of Bebop. A documentary about him is the fine movie, Straight, No Chaser.

bonuses.leadin: His compositions include "Ornithology" and "Ko-Ko." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this lowest class of people from the ancient world. Pseudolus is a clever one of these people from Roman comedy, who meddles in his household's affairs.
This Athenian comic playwright included slaves named Xanthias in his plays about Dionysus's trip to the underworld and Strepsiades's faulty education at The Thinkery.
This Roman comic playwright of Pseudolus also wrote about a braggart soldier, or Miles Gloriosus, and about two twin brothers both named Menaechmus. He lifted many plots from Menander.

bonuses.leadin: Pseudolus and Palaestrio are examples of this type of character in Greco-Roman comedy. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with muscle fiber types.
What is the main function of the sarcomere in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to muscle fiber types.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human musculoskeletal system.

parts.text: Name this gaseous element, the simplest and most common in the universe.
This is the name for the matter, mostly hydrogen, which exists between stars and star clusters. It can be mapped using the twenty-one-centimeter hydrogen line radiation.
Much of the hydrogen in the interstellar medium, especially in H-two regions, has undergone this process, in which electrons are stripped from their nuclei.

bonuses.leadin: This element's alpha emission line is a deep red color, and is part of this gas's Balmer series. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this man, who founded a namesake Indian religion and achieved enlightenment under the Bodhi tree.
The Pali Canon are the core texts of this branch of Buddhism, which is derogatorily called the "lesser vehicle," and is contrasted with Mahayana, the "greater vehicle."

Some passages of the Pali Canon are memorized and recited as a form of this spiritual practice, which is often done to promote relaxation. The Buddha achieved enlightenment by doing this under the Bodhi tree.

bonuses.leadin: The Pali Canon collects the teachings and sayings of this man, who developed the philosophy of the "Middle Way." For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this Japanese summer festival, in which people write their wishes on small pieces of paper and hang them on bamboo trees.

The Tanabata festival takes place a month before Obon, which is a day dedicated to these people. In China, food is left out for these people, and they are visited during the Qingming ["chin-ming"] Festival.

On the night before this day, Buddhist temples in Japan ring a bell 108 times. Although Japan no longer celebrates a "lunar" type of this day, China does, with practices including the gifting of money in red envelopes.

bonuses.leadin: This festival is similar to the Chinese Qixi ["chi-shi"] festival and centers on the myth of two lovers being celebrated by the Milky Way. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The region of Khao Lak ["cow-lack"] and the provinces of Phang Nga ["fang"-ah], Krabi [kraa-"bee"] and Phuket [poo-ket] suffered the greatest devastation in this country formerly known as Siam.
The 2004 tsunami was generated by an extremely powerful earthquake off the coast of Sumatra in this ocean.
The 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake was the third strongest earthquake in recorded history. The most powerful earthquake on record happened in 1960 in this South American country.

bonuses.leadin: On Dec. 26, 2004, over a dozen countries were hit by the worst tsunami [soo-NAH-mee] in recorded history, with over 230,000 people losing their lives in a matter of hours. For ten points each:

parts.text: This state of matter was first successfully created by Eric Cornell and Carl Wieman by super cooling rubidium atoms in 1995.
Bose-Einstein Condensate can only be created by cooling gas atoms to a fraction above this temperature.
At absolute zero, Bose-Einstein Condensates have this property in which waves have a uniform frequency and fixed relative phase.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about a "fifth state of matter" named for two prominent 1920s physicists, for 10 points each.

acceptableAnswers: BalletAcross Borders: Career and Culture in the World of Dancers

parts.text: Originating in Swabia during the 11th century, members of this house converted to Protestantism during the Reformation, eventually becoming Electors of Brandenburg and Kings of Prussia. Their ancestral castle is south of Stuttgart.

The Hohenzollern dynasty's greatest Enlightenment ruler was this correspondent of Voltaire and partitioner of Poland. He conquered Silesia for Prussia and was lauded by Kant for his religious tolerance.
After victory in the Franco-Prussian War, this Hohenzollern monarch was declared Emperor of Germany in 1871.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about a German dynasty, for 10 points each.

parts.text: This algorithm selects a pivot element from an array, places elements into less and greater subarrays, and then does the same on each subarray. For an array of n elements, it takes n-log-n time for an array in the average case when a pivot is chosen at random.

If quicksort is used on an already-sorted array, it performs only as well as this quadratic algorithm, which finds the minimum of an unsorted array, swaps that value with the first position, and repeats on the remaining unsorted elements.

Sometimes erroneously credited to Metzner, this is essentially a variant of insertion sort in which elements several positions apart are compared and swapped, rather than just adjacent ones. It is in big O of n log squared n.

bonuses.leadin: Name these sorting algorithms For 10 points each.
